clue.text: High hopes as good man's portion

parts.note: taken as written
PI, short for pious, is the crossword's good man; the 's is a link
a ration is an allotted portion

explanation.surface: A pious person's share of life is lofty expectation.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiration is a strong ambition, the thing one hopes for most.

clue.text: A father figure has a chesty turn

definitions.note: Father Time is pictured carrying this tool, so the phrase defines it as what he has

indicators.note: a turn is a change of form, so the letters of chesty are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A paternal figure suffers a bout of chest trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father figure' suggests a parent or mentor; here it is Father Time, the old man with an hourglass and a long-bladed tool. 'turn' rearranges CHESTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Time is traditionally drawn holding a long curved blade on a pole for reaping.

clue.text: In which there's love in bloom

definitions.text: In which there's love in bloom

parts.words: In which there's love in bloom
parts.note: love-in-... is an old name for the wild pansy, so the flower's name holds love inside the wanted word

explanation.surface: A romantic setting where love flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Oberon calls the pansy 'love-in-idleness'; the clue asks for the word that love is in, in that flower's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The flower name love-in-idleness puts love inside a word meaning sloth or inactivity.

clue.text: One big gun — in all about fifty — in the rotunda

indicators.note: the gun and the fifty go inside the word all, so in signals one piece entering another
about means surrounding, so the word all goes round the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
Big Bertha was a famous heavy German howitzer, a single big gun

explanation.surface: A big gun with about fifty men stationed inside a domed building.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Bertha was a German heavy howitzer. The rotunda is London's round concert hall in Kensington, named after Queen Victoria's consort.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous circular concert venue in South Kensington, London, is a domed rotunda.

clue.text: Look at what police officers do!

definitions.meaning: a police inspector's job, read as the verb hidden in the rank's name

explanation.surface: An instruction to observe the work of the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine is to scrutinise, and inspectors, a police rank, are named for doing just that.

clue.text: Turn on the Spanish Christmas

indicators.note: turn tells us to read the little word on in the opposite direction

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Switch on the festive celebrations in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like a verb of switching on; it reverses the little word. 'the Spanish' is a stock crossword route to the Spanish article.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël is a French-derived word for the Christmas season, familiar from carols.

clue.text: View on the box or in the canal

indicators.note: in tells us the little word or sits inside the canal's name

parts.note: the Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scene shown on television or along a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works twice: a wide view, and the long-running BBC current-affairs programme on 'the box' (British slang for television).
explanation.definitionFit: A wide unbroken vista is a sweeping view, and it is also the title of a BBC television documentary series.

clue.text: Charlatan says where Canadian riders keep their money

indicators.note: says signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.words: where Canadian riders keep their money
parts.note: the Royal Canadian Mounted Police are Mounties, so their bank is a Mountie bank

explanation.surface: A fraud claims to know where Canadian horsemen deposit their cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Canada's mounted police are called Mounties; 'Mountie bank' said quickly is the old word for a quack.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountebank was a travelling seller of fake remedies, hence any swindling impostor.

clue.text: Wine-container company turns round, makes paper

indicators.note: turns tells us to read the container and the company backwards together

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for wine
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A wine firm reverses course and goes into paper-making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses VATCO as one run to give OCTAV; O is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavo is a paper size made by folding a printed sheet into eight leaves.

clue.text: A programme, of course

parts.note: read as a programme of a course of study, not a programme that comes as no surprise

explanation.surface: Agreeing that something is a broadcast, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally'; it is literal: the programme of a course.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus outlines the topics of a course of study.

clue.text: Where someone planted Eoanthropus

parts.note: Eoanthropus, 'dawn man', was the name given to fossil remains found in a Sussex gravel pit in 1912 and later exposed as a planted hoax

explanation.surface: A question about where a forger buried a fake ancient human.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planted' means both buried and set up as a fraud: the skull was a forgery placed to be found.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sussex village gave its name to the fake 'dawn man' fossil, a famous scientific fraud.

clue.text: Goddaughter held cups

parts.note: read as the daughter of a god who held the cups, i.e. the cupbearer of Olympus, daughter of Zeus

explanation.surface: A godchild was carrying some mugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goddaughter' looks like a christening relationship; split it as god's daughter, the Greek goddess of youth who served the gods nectar.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Zeus's daughter served as cupbearer to the Olympians.

clue.text: .Sarah turns her back on men in the street, to their annoyance

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
turning her back means the name Sarah is read from end to start
in puts the men inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman snubs men loitering in the road, who are irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns her back' reverses the name; 'in' puts the men inside the street abbreviation; 'on' in a down clue sets the reversed name above. The opening dot is print noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Harassment is persistent pestering that causes distress and annoyance.

clue.text: Telegraphic record of affairs of the heart ?

definitions.text: Telegraphic record of affairs of the heart ?

parts.words: Telegraphic record of affairs of the heart
parts.note: the heart is slang 'ticker' and a recording is tape, so a record of the heart's doings is a telegraph's paper strip

explanation.surface: A telegram documenting someone's love life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affairs of the heart' suggests romance; the heart here is the ticker, as in a stock-price telegraph's printed strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker tape is the paper strip on which a telegraphic ticker printed stock prices.

clue.text: Discourse on one's previous employment ?

parts.note: ex- means former or previous
a position is a job, a post of employment

explanation.surface: A talk about the job someone used to hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on one's' is link material: a former job is an ex-position.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposition is a detailed explanation or discourse on a subject.

clue.text: Red Scotsman, with mixed USSR antecedents

indicators.note: antecedents come before, so the jumbled letters go in front of the Scotsman
mixed means the letters of USSR are jumbled

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name in crosswords

explanation.surface: A communist Scot with a mixed Soviet background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a colour; it is the Cold War word for a Soviet communist. 'antecedents' says the jumbled letters come before the Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Red was a common shorthand for a Soviet citizen or communist in the Cold War.

clue.text: Moss has maps hung awry

indicators.note: awry means out of place, so the letters of maps and hung are disordered

explanation.surface: Moss has grown over maps hanging crookedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awry' rearranges MAPS and HUNG together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sphagnum is bog moss, used in horticulture and forming peat.

clue.text: Where Swedes put up underwriting in the French manner

parts.note: taken as written
a postscript, PS, is writing added under a letter
a la is French for in the manner of

explanation.surface: Where Swedish people stay, with insurance arranged French-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underwriting' looks like insurance; it is writing underneath, a PS. 'put' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppsala is a Swedish university city north of Stockholm.

clue.text: One helping with a broken arm or a bit of shrapnel?

definitions.text: One helping with a broken arm
definitions.meaning: someone who applies a splint, read as splint plus -er
a sharp shard broken off a shell

explanation.surface: A first-aider tending a fracture, or a fragment from an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is invented: one who splints.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment of metal or wood is a sliver, and a person who fixes a splint would be a splint-er.

clue.text: Cain perhaps, or Abel; on the road

definitions.meaning: Mac means son of, and both brothers were sons of Adam

explanation.surface: Biblical brothers out travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Mac in Scottish and Irish surnames means 'son of', so a son of Adam is Mac Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: The road surface is named after John McAdam, and Adam's sons are 'Mac Adam' by the Gaelic naming pattern.

clue.text: Class-conscious period in our history

parts.note: a stage of one's own life spent in classes, not a snobbish era of the nation's past

explanation.surface: A snobbish era of national history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class-conscious' suggests social snobbery and 'our history' a national past; both are personal: lessons, and one's own life story.
explanation.definitionFit: The years of childhood spent at lessons are a period in everyone's personal history.

clue.text: Hair fastener

definitions.meaning: a tress or curl of hair
a device on a door secured with a key

explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a strand of hair, and a bolt or catch operated by key secures doors.

clue.text: Following Mum, this would be a dicey game

definitions.text: Following Mum, this would be a dicey game

parts.words: Following Mum, this would be a dicey game
parts.note: put the wanted word after Mum and you get the name of an old dice game

explanation.surface: Doing what Mother says is a risky business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dicey' means risky in the surface but literally 'played with dice': mumchance was an old dicing game.
explanation.definitionFit: Luck or risk is what drives a dice game, and mumchance was one played in silence.

clue.text: It grows in Mississippi, in Georgian loam perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a plant grown in Mississippi would thrive in Georgia's soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges IN, GA and LOAM. Mississippi is the Magnolia State, its state flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The magnolia is Mississippi's state tree and flower.

clue.text: Initially, lots of lounge lizards do so

definitions.text: Initially, lots of lounge lizards do so

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: Many idle socialites do this, to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes the first letters of LOTS OF LOUNGE LIZARDS; the whole clue also describes what idlers do.
explanation.definitionFit: Lounge lizards are idle men who sprawl and lounge about.

clue.text: I'm —— with the tide!" cried The Golden Vanity's cabin-boy

definitions.text: I'm —— with the tide!" cried The Golden Vanity's cabin-boy

parts.words: I'm —— with the tide!" cried The Golden Vanity's cabin-boy
parts.note: a fill-in quotation: in the ballad The Golden Vanity the cabin boy, left in the sea, calls that he is carried along by the tide

explanation.surface: A line from an old sea ballad about a shipwrecked boy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Golden Vanity is a traditional English ballad; the cabin boy sinks an enemy ship and is abandoned in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carried passively by the current is floating along.

clue.text: Unreal disturbance of the nerves

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so the letters of unreal are rearranged

explanation.surface: An imaginary disorder of the nervous system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' rearranges UNREAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Neural is the adjective relating to nerves or the nervous system.

clue.text: Stars are somewhat reekie in a zodiacal sign

parts.note: lum is Scots for chimney, a thing that is reekie (smoky), as in 'lang may yer lum reek'
taken as written
Aries, the ram, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Stars that seem rather smoky in one of the zodiac's signs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reekie' is Scots for smoky, as in Edinburgh's nickname Auld Reekie; a smoky Scots chimney is a LUM. 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrities and eminent people are called stars or leading lights.
